Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph OPINION NO. 14 OCT 2019 HON. RUPERT JOSEPH B. VELASCO Sangguniang Bayan Member Municipality of Paete Province of Laguna Dear SP Member Velasco: S. 20Z This has reference to your letter dated 20 June 2019, requesting the Department to render legal opinion on the following queries: i. Is it proper and allowable for a councilor to propose the passing of a resolution on First Reading while there is another resolution of the same nature and content which is already in Second Reading and was authored by another councilor? Can a councilor do this even without authority or consent of both Vice Mayor and the councilor previously tasked to author the resolution? Does mere suspension of House Rules give any councilor the right to perform such action? ii. What happens to the prior resolution that remains in Second Reading after the resolution of the same nature and content is passed on First Reading? Does the passing of the said resolution of First Reading automatically render the one in Second Reading invalid? iii. Does the Sangguniang Bayan need to make a written request to the Mayor for copies of pertinent documents requested by the Sangguniang Bayan from a Department Head or any Municipal Employee during a Committee Hearing? At the outset, in the case of Alberto Romulo vs. Nicanor Yfiiguez (141 SCRA 263) decided by the Supreme Court, internal rules do not have the force of law but are merely in the nature of by-laws prescribed for the orderly conduct of the proceedings. They are merely procedural, not substantive, thus, they may be waived or suspended by the deliberative body which created iti. The legislative process to be observed by the sanggunian are found in Sections 48-59 of the Local Government Code. Under Section 50 of the same Code, the sanggunian is given the authority to promulgate its own Internal Rules of Procedure. Accordingly, the conduct of the internal affairs of that sanggunian should be done in accordance with law, primarily, and by the adopted Internal Rules, if the law is silent2. Cited in DILG OPINION NO. 083-04, dated September 10, 2004 2 DILG OPINION NO. 136-02 dated August 22, 2002

Since it is clear that the same is not dealt with by Sections 48-59 of the Code, may we note that in the hierarchy of the sources of parliamentary rules of procedure, namely: (1) Constitution; (2) Local Government Code and other related laws; (3) Judicial Decision of the Supreme Court; (4) Internal Rules of Procedure; (5) Parliamentary Practice; (6) Parliamentary Authors; and (7) Customs and Usage3, nothing can be found from the first four sources any rule governing the issue at hand. There being none, the succession of hierarchy of sources of parliamentary rules, parliamentary practice and parliamentary authors will come in. Applying the aforesaid procedure on the issue at hand, this Department is of the view that consolidation of proposed resolutions is allowed. As a matter of fact, in the book of Professor Antonio Orendain, considered a parliamentary expert, entitled "Sanggunian Rules of Procedure", page 17, Revised Edition, it is stated that "in a proposed ordinance or resolution, resulting from a consolidation or substitution made by a committee, there shall be named as authors every member who has signed as such any of the proposed ordinances or resolution consolidated or substituted for, in the order of the names shown therein and according to the date of their filing. The scenario herein applies to query no. 2. Hence, the two resolutions may be consolidated, and that sanggunian members who are authors of the proposed Resolution should be accorded and acknowledged as such. CC: Accordingly, query nos. I and 3 are answered in the affirmative. We hope we have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: MARIVEL . SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary Dir. Elias F. Fernandez Officer-in-Charge DILG-Region IV-A (CALABARZON) Ls/90 3 DILG OPINION No. 009-09 dated 23 February 2009
